title: The Last Rivergate
premise: Petra Underhill, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate—a crew of cheerful, ruthless lenders—accepts one last job guiding a dying prospector's expedition upriver to a place called the Last Rivergate. The old man trades his map for her promise to bring everyone home and to keep silent about what they find: a drowned valley where floodwaters preserved an entire settlement, its records capable of ruining the Syndicate's founders. As the dry season shrinks the river and the Syndicate's hunters close in, Petra must choose between loyalty to her ragtag found family of expedition misfits and the truth that could free them all. In the end she leads them out through the closing rapids, exposes the Syndicate with the valley's ledgers, and pays her debt not in money but in testimony.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running freight through seasonal waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose debts—financial and otherwise—come due at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Weight of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Chasing a storm across the flats to earn hazard pay, she calculates how many more runs she needs to clear her debt to the Vane Syndicate. A near-miss lightning strike leaves her shaken and broke when her truck dies. Emotional beat: exhaustion masked as bravado; she can't afford even good luck.

chapters.title: An Offer from Cheerful Men
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Syndicate's amiable enforcer, Doss Merrick, offers to forgive half her debt if she guides an expedition for a dying prospector named Elias Wrenn. The terms are generous, which is exactly what frightens her. Emotional beat: dread dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In a hospice room smelling of rain, Elias shows Petra a hand-drawn map to the Last Rivergate and makes her swear two things: bring the crew home, and tell no one what the valley holds until he's dead and gone. She agrees because she has nothing left to lose. Emotional beat: reluctant oath-taking.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She assembles the expedition: Juno, a disgraced hydrologist; Teodor, a cook who fled three countries; and Sable, a teenage runaway who can fix anything. None of them know the destination. Emotional beat: cautious beginnings of found family.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The launch at Crooked Bend goes smoothly until Juno notices the Syndicate's survey barge shadowing them upstream data. She says nothing to Petra yet. Emotional beat: first crack of doubt; loyalty tested by observation.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Begins
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Water levels drop faster than the almanac promised, stranding them on a gravel bar for two days. Teodor feeds everyone; Sable rigs a pump; Petra realizes she'd trust these people with her life. Emotional beat: family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: What Elias Won't Say
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable catches Elias burning pages of his journal at night and pieces together that the map is older than he claims—and that someone else has been looking for the Rivergate. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Water
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Doss's men appear at a fuel cache, all smiles and questions. Petra lies well enough to buy time but understands the Syndicate knows roughly where they're headed. Emotional beat: the promise becomes a cage.

chapters.title: The Portage Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. A collapsed channel forces a brutal overland portage. Teodor injures his shoulder; Sable carries double; Juno quietly reroutes them using skills she swore she'd buried. Emotional beat: competence as redemption.

chapters.title: Elias Fades
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sick and failing, Elias tells Petra fragments: the valley flooded in a single night forty years ago, and the Syndicate's founders were there. He begs her to remember that some truths are heavier than debts. Emotional beat: passing of the torch mid-journey.

chapters.title: The Gate Itself
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They round the final bend and find it: a limestone arch spanning a shrinking river, beyond it a valley the maps erased. First sight of the drowned town's rooftops breaking the receding waterline. Emotional beat: awe that feels like trespass.

chapters.title: Belltown Below
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Exploring the preserved settlement, Juno finds the church records vault—intact, sealed, damning. The ledgers name the Syndicate's founders as the men who dynamited the levee to drown the town and its claims. Emotional beat: horror wearing the face of history.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Vault
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra holds the ledgers and understands their power: proof that could destroy the Syndicate or be sold back to it. She keeps the promise and orders the vault resealed, lying to the crew about what they found. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized into secrecy.

chapters.title: Sable Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable watched Petra seal the vault and confronts her privately. Petra gives her only part of the truth. Sable, abandoned by adults before, decides to trust her anyway—the story's emotional hinge. Emotional beat: faith as a deliberate act.

chapters.title: Doss Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Syndicate's boats arrive in force. Doss offers Petra full forgiveness for the ledgers; behind him, men check their rifles casually. She stalls, promising delivery by season's end, hating how easily the lie forms. Emotional beat: bargaining with wolves.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Fire
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. That night the crew demands answers. Petra finally tells them everything except Elias's secret clause. Juno wants to sell the ledgers; Teodor wants to burn them; Sable backs Petra. The family fractures over the fire. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: Elias Dies at the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias dies at dawn beneath the arch, asking only that Petra finish it her way. Grief strips the argument down to essentials: he trusted her, not the ledgers. Emotional beat: mourning that clarifies rather than confuses.

chapters.title: The Rising Water Trick
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno proposes a gambit: use the last storm of the season to raise the river, float the expedition out past the Syndicate blockade, and deliver the ledgers to a federal magistrate downstream instead of to Doss. Emotional beat: hope engineered from desperation.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Riding the storm surge, they shoot the rapids under gunfire. Teodor takes a graze; Sable steers them through the arch one last time; Doss's boat wrecks on the shallows his own employers caused. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into triumph.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the magistrate's office in Harrow Ford, Petra surrenders the ledgers and testifies, erasing her debt by ending the lender. The Syndicate's founders are indicted; Doss, arrested, almost admires her. Emotional beat: truth paid out at last, at full weight.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Weeks later, the state seals the valley as a memorial. The crew visits the arch together—no longer employer and hires, but family. Sable reflects on choosing trust once and being right. Emotional beat: quiet gratitude.

chapters.title: The Next Storm
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra sells her debt-ridden truck, buys a proper expedition boat with her testimony bounty, and signs on to guide Juno's research survey. When the first storm cells build on the horizon, she points the bow toward them—not fleeing, not hiding, just going home the long way. Emotional beat: freedom found in forward motion.
